what.body: GybeLock lets you drop windsurfing videos into a local folder, automatically processes them in the background, and lets you review them later in a smooth player.

cannotOpen.answer: Only jobs with status “succeeded” can be opened. If it’s processing, wait a moment and refresh.
cannotOpen.question: Why can’t I open a video yet?

deleteAccount.answer: Open the Analyzer, click Settings, then click Delete account.
deleteAccount.question: How do I delete my account?

fileNotFound.answer: The player opens videos from your local ingress folder. If the file can’t be located, select the correct folder again (Ingress → Change folder) and make sure the video still exists in that folder.
fileNotFound.question: Why does the player say “VIDEO FILE NOT FOUND”?

formats.answer: MP4 is recommended. If you encounter issues, try re-exporting to H.264 MP4.
formats.question: What formats are supported?

ingressFolder.answer: It’s a folder on your computer that GybeLock monitors periodically. When you drop a new video in it, GybeLock will automatically upload it for processing.
ingressFolder.question: What is the ingress folder?

movedVideo.answer: If the moved/renamed file can’t be found, the player may show VIDEO FILE NOT FOUND. Put the video back into the ingress folder (or expected subfolder) and make sure the correct ingress folder is selected.
movedVideo.question: I moved or renamed a video. What should I do?

processedVideos.answer: They appear in the Analyzer grid as soon as a job is finished. Click a tile to open the player.
processedVideos.question: Where do processed videos appear?

shortcuts.answer: In the Analyzer / Player, click Shortcuts to open the keyboard shortcuts modal.
shortcuts.question: How do I see all keyboard controls?

supportedFootage.answer: GybeLock is designed for shore / beach-shot videos (tele/zoom from land). MP4 is recommended. GoPro/action-cam POV footage is not supported / not the intended use case.
supportedFootage.question: What footage is supported?

uploadSkipped.answer: GybeLock deduplicates videos by checksum. If that exact video was already uploaded/processed, it may be skipped.
uploadSkipped.question: Why was my upload skipped?

uploadsPaused.answer: Open Ingress and check the error message. If uploads paused after a failure, use Retry failed. If you see a beta feedback request message, please reach out to us.
uploadsPaused.question: Uploads are paused / stuck. What can I do?

videoTooLong.answer: There is a maximum supported video length. If your upload fails with “Video too long”, split the recording into shorter clips and upload those.
videoTooLong.question: Why does upload say “Video too long”?

whatDoes.answer: GybeLock helps you review beach-shot windsurf footage (shore camera, long zoom) by stabilizing the footage, detecting/tracking riders, and letting you click a rider to get a smooth, focused view for review.

bullets.account: Account data: email address, Firebase user ID (UID), email verification status.
bullets.analytics: Usage analytics (optional): if you consent, Google Analytics collects page views and click events (e.g., “ui_click”, “analysis_upload_start”).
bullets.jobs: Job / processing data: job IDs, timestamps, processing status, error messages, and the generated tracking results (e.g., tracks/segments) needed to show you analysis.
bullets.logs: Technical logs: IP address and request logs may be processed by our hosting/providers to operate and secure the Service.
bullets.uploads: Uploaded video data (temporary): video files you upload for processing; file name, MIME type, file size; checksums (e.g., SHA-256) used for deduplication. Videos are only processed and then deleted; they are not stored long-term.

data.noteIngress: Note: GybeLock also uses a local “ingress folder” on your device. Selecting a folder and playing a local file happens on your device; uploads only occur when you add videos and the Analyzer uploads them for processing.
data.noteSettings: The Service also stores some settings locally in your browser (e.g., your analytics consent choice).

what.body1: GybeLock is a windsurf-session review tool focused on finding and reviewing gybes/jibes (or other moments where a rider is visible) by automatically detecting and tracking surfers in your uploaded videos.
what.body2: Typical workflow: you record a session (shore / beach tele footage), drop raw MP4 files into a designated folder, GybeLock uploads and processes them, and you review the finished results by jumping between tracked rider segments.
what.body3: This is a small-scale, donation-supported project and may be offered as a beta service.
what.title: 2. What GybeLock does
